Upper bounds — holds for every total

  • \(\hat L_1(f) \le \mathrm{DTsize}(f)\)
    ODonnell14
    Write $f$ as a sum over the leaves of an optimal tree, $f = \sum_{\ell} f(\ell)\,\mathbb{1}_{C_\ell}$, one term per leaf subcube. A subcube indicator of codimension $d$ factors as $\prod_{i \in S}\tfrac{1 \pm x_i}{2}$ over its $d$ fixed coordinates, so its spectral norm is $1$; the triangle inequality adds them up. With $|f(\ell)| = 1$ this is $\hat L_1(f) \le \#\{\text{leaves}\}$.

Lower bounds / separations — there is a family achieving this

  • \(\hat L_1(\mathrm{ADDR}_k) = 2^k = \tfrac12\,\mathrm{DTsize}(\mathrm{ADDR}_k)\)
    witness: \(\mathrm{ADDR}_k\)
    Every certificate of $\mathrm{ADDR}_k$ has size $k+1$, so every leaf sits at depth $\ge k+1$ and the tree has $2^{k+1}$ of them; the spectral norm is $2^k$. A factor $2$ from the bound, and the only slack in it.

The leaf argument proves this, and the familiar $\hat L_1 \le 2^{\mathrm{D}}$ is its corollary via $\mathrm{DTsize} \le 2^{\mathrm{D}}$ -- worth keeping the order straight, because size is the quantity the proof actually counts and a wide shallow tree makes the difference enormous: \(\mathrm{OMB}_n\) has $\hat L_1 = \Theta(n) = \Theta(\mathrm{DTsize})$ but $2^{\mathrm{D}} = 2^n$.

see also: \(\hat{L}_1(f)\), \(\mathrm{DTsize}(f)\), \(\mathrm{D}(f)\), \(\mathrm{spar}(f)\), \(\mathrm{ADDR}_k\), \(\mathrm{OMB}_n\) data/relations/05-fourier.yaml

facts: $\hat L_1(f)\le 2^{\mathrm{D}(f)}$ (sum the leaf indicators), and $\hat L_1(f)\ge 1$ always.
Bounds of the form $\mathrm{D}^{\oplus}(f) = O(\hat L_1(f)^2)$ hold; sharpening them is tied to the log-rank conjecture.

Relations of the shape $\deg_2(f)\le \log_2(\mathrm{spar}(f)+1)$ connect $\hat L_1$, $\mathrm{spar}$ and degree. Note it is the $\mathbb{F}_2$-degree: the real degree is not bounded by sparsity at all, since $\chi_{[n]}$ has $\deg = n$ and $\mathrm{spar} = 1$.
For approximate versions, $\widetilde{\deg}(f)$ and $\hat L_{1,\varepsilon}(f)$ are the query analogues of approximate rank / approximate $\gamma_2$ in communication complexity.
